sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the technical requirements for the Hospital EMR Patient Management System (Patient Portal). The document serves as a baseline for design, implementation, and verification.

### 1.2 Scope
The system is a web-based portal integrated with the hospital's Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system, allowing patients to view their health data and manage appointments. 

### 1.3 Definitions
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record.
- **PHI**: Protected Health Information.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
The Patient Portal operates as a secure web application. It interfaces with the core EMR database to retrieve patient-specific data. The architecture must ensure strict isolation of patient data and secure transmission channels. 

*Note: Detailed architectural diagrams and specific database schemas are not provided in the source document and are flagged as open items requiring stakeholder input.*

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: System shall support secure user login for patients.
System shall fetch patient records from the EMR upon request.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements (Performance, Security, Reliability mapped to domain standards)
sections.body:
### 4.1 Performance
- **SRS-NFR-001**: The system shall maintain a P95 latency of < 250ms for standard data retrieval operations, per healthcare domain NFR benchmarks.

### 4.2 Security (HIPAA Compliance)
- **SRS-NFR-002 (Encryption at Rest)**: All Protected Health Information (PHI) stored in the database or on file systems must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or an equivalent standard, per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv).
- **SRS-NFR-003 (Audit Logging)**: The system shall implement comprehensive audit logging for all access to PHI. Logs must record the user ID, timestamp, and specific data accessed, and must be tamper-evident, per HIPAA §164.312(b).

### 4.3 Reliability
- *Open Item*: Specific uptime and failover requirements are not defined in the source document and require stakeholder input.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements (APIs, UI, Hardware)
sections.body:
### 5.1 User Interface
The system shall provide a responsive web interface for patient interaction.

### 5.2 System Interfaces
The system shall communicate with the Hospital EMR via a secure API.

*Note: Specific API protocols (e.g., HL7 FHIR, REST) and hardware dependencies are not specified in the source document and are open items.*

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
### 6.1 Compliance
The system must strictly adhere to HIPAA regulations regarding the privacy and security of electronic PHI.

### 6.2 Constraints
- Data residency constraints are not specified in the source document.
- Technology stack constraints are not specified in the source document.
